hero.title: The writing studio for novelists that you can actually run yourself.
hero.subtitle: Write in the browser, get an AI editor that knows your whole book — using your own API key — export retail-ready EPUB and PDF, and track your royalties. AGPL-licensed, self-hostable, and yours to modify.
hero.license: Free and open source under the AGPL-3.0. No account required to self-host.

faq.heading: Common questions.
faq.q1: Do I need to pay for anything?
faq.a1: No. The whole application is AGPL-3.0 licensed and self-hostable. The only thing that costs money is AI inference, and you pay your provider directly with your own API key — nothing routes through us. Everything except the AI features works with no key at all.
faq.q2: What do I need to run it?
faq.a2: Just Docker. One command starts the app, its Postgres database and the export service on your own machine, with no cloud account of any kind. See the self-hosting guide in the repository for the full walkthrough.
faq.q3: What happens to my manuscript when I use the AI features?
faq.a3: It is sent to whichever model provider you configured, processed, and discarded. This application never logs, caches, or persists manuscript text sent to an AI API, and never uses it for training. Because you supply your own key, your data relationship is directly with the provider under their terms — read them.
faq.q4: Can I use it without any AI at all?
faq.a4: Yes, and that is the default. With no API key configured the AI surfaces are simply inert; the editor, importer, formatter, exporter, and royalty tracker all work normally.
faq.q5: What does the AGPL mean for me?
faq.a5: You can run, study, modify, and share it freely. If you modify it and offer it to others over a network, you must offer them your modified source too. For personal or in-house use there is nothing extra to do.
faq.a6: Yes — the entire interface and the editorial AI prompts ship in English and Mexican Spanish, and the two locales are kept at exact key parity. Adding a third locale is a documented contribution path.

pillars.p1Body: A real manuscript editor in the browser: chapter navigation, drag-and-drop reordering, split and merge, find and replace, writing stats, and autosave with version history. Import your existing .docx or .txt.
pillars.p2Body: An AI editor that has read your whole book — editorial reports, style analysis, continuity checks, and a chat assistant grounded in your chapters. Bring your own API key, so the inference bill is yours and the manuscript never touches our servers.
pillars.p3Body: Genre-matched CSS templates rendered to EPUB 3 and print-ready PDF by a Pandoc + WeasyPrint service you run alongside the app. Accessibility metadata included.
pillars.p4Body: Import royalty CSVs from KDP, Apple, Kobo, and StreetLib into one earnings view with per-title revenue charts. No aggregator, no cut, no lock-in.

about.heading: About ManuHaven
about.body: ManuHaven is an open-source writing studio for novelists: a browser manuscript editor, an AI editor that works from your own API key, EPUB and PDF export, and royalty tracking. It began as a commercial publishing platform and was opened up instead — the publishing business was cut, and the studio is what remained worth keeping. It is AGPL-3.0 licensed, self-hostable, and developed in the open. Contributions and bug reports are welcome on GitHub.

contact.heading: Contact
contact.body: Development happens in the open on GitHub. Open an issue for bugs and feature requests, or start a discussion for self-hosting help and general questions — both get a faster answer than email, and the answer stays useful to the next person. For security reports, please follow the private disclosure process in SECURITY.md rather than filing a public issue.

privacy.heading: Privacy
privacy.body: When you self-host ManuHaven, your data lives in your own database and nobody else can see it — there is no telemetry and no phone-home. This notice covers the hosted demo only. The demo stores the account and manuscripts you create so the app can function, and demo accounts are deleted after seven days. AI features require your own API key; manuscript text sent to a model provider is processed and discarded, never logged, never cached, and never used for training. Because the key is yours, your data relationship for that text is directly with the provider under their terms. Optional analytics are disabled unless a PostHog key is configured. When enabled they record only named product events, with no automatic click capture and no session recordings, and never include manuscript content.
